function: MBACNN (attention, CNN, MLP) jointly selects discrete RIS phases and a codebook TX precoder from CSI, maximizing SNR or sum rate (pp. 3-7).
system: MISO: 16-antenna TX (also 32), DFT codebook, single-antenna RX, reflecting RIS with 400-1600 1-bit elements (also 3-bit, multi-user, 2-4 RISs); 28 GHz in DeepMIMO tests (pp. 3, 11-13).
method: Multi-branch attention CNN with per-element MLP, trained offline by neuroevolution (CoSyNE genetic algorithm, gradient-free), fitness equals average SNR over episodes; distributed multi-RIS extension with shared parameters (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Custom stochastic simulator: RIS-RX Ricean (kappa 10 dB), blocked direct link; plus DeepMIMO O1 outdoor scenario, BS 3 as TX, BS 8 as RIS, 28 GHz (p. 11).
test_conditions: Evolved offline on simulated episodes, tested on 20 extra episodes (1,000 channels); one mismatch test adds AWGN to the RIS-RX channel; no unseen scenario or site (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Learned: A2C DRL agent, NE-optimized feedforward NN (NE-FF); non-learned: lightweight genetic algorithm (LGA), block exhaustive search (BES); centralized NE-FF for multi-RIS (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Ergodic achievable rate (bps/Hz), average received SNR (dB), sum rate, SNR standard deviation in sensitivity study, forward-pass time in ms, trainable parameters (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Forward-pass complexity O((NTX+NRX)NRIS^2) (p. 7); fewer than 9.2e5 weights versus 1.2e8 for NE-FF and about 12M for A2C (p. 10); forward-pass time 0.2-0.7 ms, Table I (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "sampling channel realizations from the outdoor" DeepMIMO O1 scenario, with "a narrowband carrier at 28 GHz was used"; Fig. 5 (p. 12) reports results on these channels. The stochastic Ricean setup of Section VI-B is custom.
q2_support: p. 13: "capture the mismatch of channel parameters between the training and evaluation environments, and may additionally be thought to be akin to channel-estimation-induced errors" (one AWGN perturbation of h2, same DeepMIMO scenario); p. 11: other sweeps are "after the completion of each training procedure". No new scenario, band, or site; counted as a CSI-error test.
q3_support: p. 10: "the DRL agent as [27], [28], an FF NE-based agent, and two classical discrete optimization schemes" (A2C, NE-FF, LGA, BES); p. 11: "greatly outperforms all benchmarks under all P values" (Fig. 4a, rate).
q4_support: p. 7: "The asymptotic computational complexity of a forward pass of our proposed MBACNN architecture" is O((NTX+NRX)NRIS^2); p. 11: "Table I demonstrates that this time, measured in msec, exhibits sub-linear scaling with increasing NRIS".
q5_support: p. 11: "sampling channel realizations from the outdoor" DeepMIMO O1 scenario (public dataset [65], p. 15), used for the geometric-channel results. No code or data release link appears in pp. 1-15.
notes: Includes with area 3: the learned decision is the RIS phase configuration plus the TX precoder choice. q1 and q5 rest on the DeepMIMO experiments of Section VI-C; the stochastic experiments of VI-B, VI-D, VI-E use a custom Ricean simulator. q2 is borderline for the reviewer: p. 12-13 calls the AWGN test generalization to slightly different testing environments, and p. 11 says the kappa sweep (Fig. 4b) investigates generalization across channel conditions, but it also evaluates after each training procedure, so no model trained in one condition is clearly tested in another. Table I and figure legends were read as images of pp. 11-12.
